subject: Priv infra review: service chaining + multihome routing + CI/iAC idempotency
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Young <alice@acmehealth.com>, Bob Park <bob.procure@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priv infra review: service chaining + multihome routing + CI/iAC idempotency

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the call last week. Attached is an early architecture sketch that consolidates the items we discussed: service chaining across the customer VLANs (east/west routing for model inferencing traffic), support for two upstream ISPs in multihome (BGP/eBGP at the edge), and a proposed MVLAN zoning for management vs inference lanes.

As we're preparing the IaC bundle for your on-prem validation, two asks to help us narrow the checklist before the formal security evidence review: 

- Can you confirm whether the on-prem edge device will be running BGP or if you'll prefer a layer-3 routing appliance we manage (we can do either; BGP gives more automated failover but requires ASN coordination).
- Any constraints on IP addressing (RFC1918 blocks) we must respect for your internal L2/L3 zoning?
- Do you have a preferred method for outbound egress auditing (mirror to your SIEM vs S3 shipper)?

From our side I'm asking the infra team to run a targeted idempotency check against Ansible playbooks and verify Terraform state locking across both the management and inference workspaces. Karthik / Irene — I've flagged you for two short deliverables: an Ansible idempotency recap and a CI preflight patch that gates merge requests on terraform-plan/helm-dryrun success.

Attachments: priv-architecture-draft.pdf (diagram + variable matrix)

I'll set up a quick 30-min walkthrough next week if that helps.

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Principal Cloud Engineer — Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Priv infra review: service chaining + multihome routing + CI/iAC idempotency

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for the draft. A few quick notes from our network team: 

- We prefer to keep BGP at the customer edge; our firewall team will provide the ASN and speaking policies.
- Addressing: we can allocate a /22 for the inference VLANs and will reserve a /24 for management. I'll share the exact ranges in a follow-up spreadsheet.
- For egress auditing, we need both SIEM forward (syslog) and an object-store sink for raw pcap exports.

I've attached the procurement scope (lightweight) for the initial order and a rough timeline; procurement questions will be directed to Bob (cc).

Would the team be able to run the Ansible idempotency checks against a staging snapshot? We cannot have changes to the management VLAN cause additional interruptions.

Thanks,
Alice Young
Director of IT Operations — Acme Health
alice@acmehealth.com
Attachment: acme-procurement-scope.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Young <alice@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra review: service chaining + multihome routing + CI/iAC idempotency

Chloe / team —

I've run a quick idempotency sweep against the Ansible roles we plan to use in the management plane. High-level observations: 

1) Most roles are idempotent for package installs and service unit files. 
2) We have three playbooks that mutate device-specific facts (interface naming, SR-IOV PCI slots) where the current handlers trigger restarts on every run due to templated if statements. Those need guard clauses (changed_when / check_mode blocks) to be truly idempotent.
3) Helm releases are fine if we avoid hooks that mutate namespace-level CRDs during sync. Current chart for the model-router includes a post-install hook to bootstrap a CRD; we should move CRD creation into a preflight job.
4) Terraform: state locking is fine for single-region workspaces, but our intended separation (management.tfstate + inference.tfstate) requires cross-workspace dependencies to be expressed via outputs pushed to a state-bucket; we'll also need to ensure remote-state locking (consul or S3/dynamo) is enabled for the orchestration account.

I've attached a short report that annotates the failing tasks and suggests quick remediation (ansible-idempotency-report.md) and a tf-state-locking-checklist.txt with recommended remote backends.

Action items I propose: 
- Add changed_when guards on 3 tasks in network roles (Irene).
- Move model-router CRD bootstrap to CI preflight (Karthik).
- Add a terraform plan job that fails the MR if any drift is detected against the management workspace (Vanessa).

I can sign up for the first item this week.

--
Irene Choi
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Young <alice@acmehealth.com>, Bob Park <bob.procure@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra review: service chaining + multihome routing + CI/iAC idempotency

Thanks for the notes — good catch on the CRD hook. I sketched a small CI patch that: 

- Adds "ci/terraform-plan-management" and "ci/helm-dryrun-modelrouter" jobs to the GitLab pipeline (must pass before merge).
- Runs ansible --check on a staging snapshot job that uses the vagrant-like containerized test harness.
- Validates remote-state locks via a short script that calls the S3/Dynamo lock API and fails if locks cannot be acquired.

I'll upload a patch containing the pipeline changes and a preflight script; if we gate merges in the privdeploy repo we'll catch the CRD bootstrap issues before anything lands.

Patch: gitlab-ci-preflight.patch (contains job definitions + a small helper script).

Related MR: https://gitlab.redwood.internal/privdeploy/merge_requests/312 — please review the job names and the failure conditions; I intentionally made the terraform-plan step strict for the management workspace to avoid accidental drift.

If Alice / Acme wants us to run the full sweep against a copy of their staging inventory, we'll need the inventory export (IP ranges + device credentials) in the secure vault. Bob — can procurement surface a short credential transfer method?

Karthik
Staff Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Priv infra review: service chaining + multihome routing + CI/iAC idempotency

Team —

Solid progress. Quick summary and next steps for tracking: 

1) Irene: please submit the ansible fixes as a small PR (three guarded tasks) by EOD Monday. Include test cases that verify no-op changes in check_mode.
2) Karthik: open the MR for the CI preflight (MR 312 is fine) and add a short README describing the failure semantics; we'll pin the pipeline to require yes/no on the management workspace.
3) Vanessa: add the terraform-remote-state docs to the privdeploy runbook and ensure the lock-check script is included in the preflight image.
4) Alice / Bob: when you can share the exact IP allocations and the credential handoff method we will run the staging sweep.

I'll schedule a 30-min session next Tuesday (2027-06-22 10:00 PT) for a live walkthrough and to capture evidence items for your security checklist.

Attachments included in thread: priv-architecture-draft.pdf, ansible-idempotency-report.md, tf-state-locking-checklist.txt, gitlab-ci-preflight.patch

Thanks everyone — this keeps us on track for the targeted July sprints.

Best,
Chloe
